def hidden_rule_fn(state):
    # Compute next state based on diagonal-tetrad counts
    # For each cell, count d_z (0s), d_p (1s), d_q (2s) in diagonal neighbors
    # Next state = majority value (highest count, ties broken by preferring 2 > 1 > 0)
    
    rows = len(state)
    cols = len(state[0])
    next_state = [[0] * cols for _ in range(rows)]
    
    for r in range(rows):
        for c in range(cols):
            # Compute diagonal-tetrad with toroidal wrapping
            neighbors = [
                state[(r - 1) % rows][(c - 1) % cols],  # NW
                state[(r - 1) % rows][(c + 1) % cols],  # NE
                state[(r + 1) % rows][(c - 1) % cols],  # SW
                state[(r + 1) % rows][(c + 1) % cols],  # SE
            ]
            
            # Count each value
            d_z = sum(1 for v in neighbors if v == 0)
            d_p = sum(1 for v in neighbors if v == 1)
            d_q = sum(1 for v in neighbors if v == 2)
            
            # Find majority value (highest count, ties broken by preferring 2 > 1 > 0)
            counts = [(d_q, 2), (d_p, 1), (d_z, 0)]
            counts.sort(reverse=True)
            next_state[r][c] = counts[0][1]
    
    return next_state
